entrypoints.summary: The documented OPA server accepts an HTTP PUT to /v1/data/roles; the report states its endpoints were unrestricted in the assessed default/tutorial deployment.

negative_controls: Before alteration, the report states the test user is not in the admin group and cannot execute sudo.
The report does not provide an execution transcript or a tested restricted-endpoint control result.
observability.positive_marker: The report states that after dataset corruption the test user can execute sudo.

preconditions: The deployment uses OPA with PAM for sudo authorization.
OPA endpoint access is unrestricted as in the assessed default/tutorial configuration.
The attacker can reach the OPA server HTTP endpoint and is a user whose sudo authorization depends on the role dataset.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A JSON object setting admin to an array containing ops and test.
trigger_steps.summary: Send an HTTP PUT to /v1/data/roles with a roles object whose admin list includes the attacker account test.

impacts.concept: Root-level host command execution through sudo

mitigations.concept: Authenticated and authorized OPA endpoint access

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states unrestricted OPA endpoints allow a regular user to corrupt the dataset, and provides a PUT request to the roles endpoint.
The supplied PUT adds test to the admin role, after which the report says the test user can execute sudo.

relation_candidates.dst: Root-level host command execution through sudo
relation_candidates.rationale: The report characterizes obtaining sudo capability in this default PAM setup as escalation to root privileges.

relation_candidates.dst: Authenticated and authorized OPA endpoint access
relation_candidates.rationale: The report recommends using the endpoint-restriction mechanism and considering token/basic authentication by default, which prevents an unprivileged caller from performing the mutation.

impact.affected_asset: Host sudo authorization and the integrity of the OPA role dataset used for PAM policy decisions.
impact.attacker_capability: A regular test user can gain the ability to execute sudo, described by the report as root-privilege escalation in the assessed PAM deployment.
impact.security_effect: Privilege escalation through an attacker-modified authorization decision

causal_trace.summary: The assessed PAM/sudo deployment delegates policy checks to an OPA server and uses a role dataset in which the admin group normally contains only the ops user.
OPA endpoint access is unrestricted, so a regular user can write authorization data that determines membership in the privileged admin role.
A PUT request to /v1/data/roles supplies an admin list containing both ops and test, corrupting the dataset subsequently used for authorization.
After the dataset mutation, the test user can execute sudo; the report describes this as escalation to root privileges in the documented setup.

failure.operation: HTTP PUT mutation of the OPA role dataset at /v1/data/roles

primary_invariant.kind: authorization-data integrity and control-plane access control
primary_invariant.statement: Only authorized administrators may modify the OPA role dataset that PAM/OPA policy evaluation uses to grant sudo authorization.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The documented configuration does not restrict OPA endpoints, allowing a regular user to PUT a role dataset that adds their account to the admin group.

raw_refs.role: finding report, PoC, deployment scope, and recommendation

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report supplies the deployment model, exact PUT payload shape, stated authorization outcome, and configuration/documentation recommendations. No immutable historical OPA source revision, maintainer patch, fixed-version scope, regression test, or captured execution transcript is supplied. Scope is limited to the documented PAM/sudo deployment with unrestricted OPA endpoints, not all OPA deployments or an inherent implementation defect.

remediation.invariant_restored: Role and policy data that influence PAM/sudo decisions can be changed only through restricted OPA endpoints by authorized administrators.
mitigation_classes: authenticate and authorize policy/data management endpoints

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The report's test user is initially outside the admin group and cannot execute sudo; the attacker submits a role-dataset update that adds test to admin.
data_structure_invariants: The admin role list must remain writable only by authorized administrators.
PAM/OPA sudo authorization must consume role data whose integrity has not been modified by a subject seeking authorization.
state_context.state_machine: A PAM sudo request is evaluated against OPA role data; an unrestricted OPA data-management request can alter that role data before a later sudo authorization evaluation.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Default/tutorial PAM-for-sudo deployment assessed by Cure53, report dated 2018-08-30; no immutable affected OPA source revision or fixed version is established.

target.component: OPA server endpoint-access configuration and role dataset used by the documented PAM/sudo authorization deployment

oracle.channel: HTTP request followed by sudo authorization behavior
oracle.expected_negative: With endpoint access restricted so an unprivileged user cannot modify the role dataset, the mutation request should not change that user's sudo authorization.
oracle.expected_positive: Against the documented unrestricted deployment, PUT /v1/data/roles with test added to admin changes the reported test-user outcome to being able to execute sudo.
